We present TouchTwin, a human-AI approach that turns phone scans of tabletop scenes into editable haptic scenes. TouchTwin uses AI to propose material regions that users can experience and revise through language and spatial edits. A model trained on measured tool-surface interactions generates the haptic responses, allowing users to work with material descriptions rather than low-level signal parameters. In a study with N=12 participants and physical reference objects present, automatic drafts scored 4.0/7 for realism and 5.4/7 as useful starting points. After a median of 6.6 minutes of editing, realism increased to 5.6/7, while scoring the saved material layers against ground truth showed material-family accuracy improving from 52% to 92%. Participants also used the same workflow to author material feels without a physical reference.

papers.title: Particle Selection in Virtual Reality
papers.abstract: Point-cloud representations of 3D data are used in many fields, from astronomical surveys of galaxies to medical imaging and laser scans of buildings. A task common to all of these is interactive selection: picking out a meaningful subset of points for closer analysis. The data is inherently 3D, yet the traditional workflow uses a 2D mouse on a 2D projection and inherits the limitations of a flat screen. This paper compares Virtual Reality (VR) and desktop environments for 3D particle selection, asking whether VR's six-degree-of-freedom hand interaction yields measurable gains in accuracy, speed, usability, workload and flow. In a counterbalanced within-subjects experiment (N = 34), participants selected 90 target galaxies from a catalogue of 16,816 galaxies, using mouse-driven selection with keyboard camera control on the desktop and a hand-held spherical brush that adds or removes particles in VR. We measured task accuracy, completion time, and three standard questionnaires: the System Usability Scale (SUS), the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) and the Flow State Scale (FSS). Accuracy was comparable (91.6% VR vs. 93.1% desktop; p = 0.858), but every other measure favoured VR. Tasks were 23% faster (p = 0.001, d = 0.93), usability was higher (SUS 84.6 vs. 54.0; d = -1.78), workload was lower (NASA-TLX 20.4 vs. 34.7; d = 0.90), and flow was higher (FSS 83.2 vs. 70.2; d = -1.23). Because the underlying problem, making a 3D selection through a 2D interface, is not specific to astronomy, we expect the pattern to carry over to point-cloud selection in other fields.

papers.title: Better together? A performance theory of human-machine skill policies under generalization difficulty
papers.abstract: Organizations pairing a human and a machine on a task decide, often by default, which executes each instance and what happens when both do. We account for what this attains under the squared rule, with performance distributed over instances to capture generalization difficulty. A gross stake lies between the skills' mean and best per instance. It splits at the best single skill into a systematic part, known from separate assessments and secured by commitment, and a residual, the expected value of perfect information on which skill each instance favors, known only from paired observation and split further by classes. Skills set the stake; workflows decide the take, via two channels. Routing directs work, weighting or selecting responses; with binary truth it is capped by the best skill per instance. Reading responses as joint evidence is not routing; what they jointly reveal caps it. Synergy lets skills interact before responding; bounded by no skill either way, its lift over independent responses must clear a break-even and can fall below one. As algorithms, arrangements form a ladder stating what each reads, holds and records, and a procedure whose checks keep earlier gains when class means are known and lose little on finite records given a margin. The theory extends to many skills, each worth what it adds where it beats all others held, and to competing skills, where at parity a single failure's allowed cost decides. In a public chest-radiograph study with 227 radiologists, they are near parity with the model and the stake is mostly residual; assisted reading, no better on average originally, returned less than averaging both responses; recalibrating the model alone beats any deployable arrangement of raw responses. Organizations can learn from their records what is at stake, which arrangement collects it and what evidence each step needs; pricing costs and errors is future work.

papers.title: Integrating Feature Understandability into Feature Selection for Human-Centred Tabular Explanations
papers.abstract: Existing human-centred XAI research predominantly evaluates explanations after they have been generated. However, this fails to provide actionable insights into improving accessibility. This study incorporates human-based feature understandability into feature selection to improve the generation of human-centred explanations. Natural language explanations for machine learning models trained on tabular data often cite influential features in the input data to explain a given decision. As a consequence, users' ability to understand the produced explanation hinges on their understanding of the cited features. To quantify this natural-language feature understandability, Rossberg et al. proposed the Feature Understandability Scale, which assigns numerical `understandability scores' to features based on user feedback. To evaluate the degree to which these scores can improve machine learning explanation quality, this study collects understandability scores across two datasets, proposes an understandability-aware feature selection algorithm to select features that are both understandable and informative, and trains a random forest based on these feature subsets. The SHAP-based explanations generated by this model are evaluated using user feedback, and changes in explanation quality are assessed. The individual evaluation of the explanations showed that while the understandability-based explanations scored higher on average, the difference was not statistically significant. In contrast, the comparative evaluation found that participants preferred these explanations significantly more frequently than expected at the chance level. It is concluded that the integration of understandability can yield more understandable explanations at minimal cost to classification performance, although changes to quality require elucidation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Foresee: Making Procedural Futures Tangible through Generative Previews
papers.abstract: Procedural guidance can show users how to act without explaining what an action enables later. We present Foresee, an interface combining next-step guidance with consequence previews, method comparisons, and cross-step access. A hybrid pipeline combines structured rendering, image editing, and video generation. A literature-informed framework and six-participant formative study shaped its design. A 24-participant study compared AR guidance, AR with generated video, and Foresee across digital painting, gameplay, and cocktail making. Exploratory painting comparisons showed higher correct completion without a recorded error than AR and higher post-task quiz accuracy than generated-video guidance under task-wise correction. Interviews revealed that users could overlook valued explanations, match visible outcomes without understanding later possibilities, or wait for concrete demonstrations when symbolic cues were unclear. These findings inform generative previews that explain what actions enable or constrain while supporting ongoing execution.

papers.title: What UI Design Can Do For "Good" Oversight Work: A Three-Month Action Research Study
papers.abstract: With AI automating consequential tasks, human oversight is required for ethical, legal, and practical reasons. Yet these oversight tasks can be demanding and often make for poor work. Empirical evidence on overseers' lived work experiences remains underexplored, yet critical for designing ``good'' oversight. We provide longitudinal, in-the-wild insights through action research accompanying (N=8) tutors who oversaw an AI-supported learning assistant over three months. Our thematic analysis combines insights from twelve weekly meetings and two workshop iterations and was enriched by four repeated questionnaires. We identified stimulation, mastery, and relatedness as key challenges, stemming from the task's repetitiveness, unclear impact of interventions, and limited connections with students and peers. Informed by our initial findings, we deployed targeted UI modifications with mixed success. This paper documents the long-term evolution of the work characteristics of a real-world oversight task and discusses which oversight work characteristics can and cannot be supported by interface design.

papers.title: STEPwise: Supporting Teachers in Diagnosing Students' Mathematical Problem-Solving Skills through LLM-Generated Questions and Rubric
papers.abstract: Problem-solving is central to mathematics education. However, diagnosing where students' reasoning breaks down requires individualized probing and consistent criteria that teachers cannot sustain at classroom scale. We introduce STEP (STage-based Evaluation of Problem-solving skills), co-designed with six mathematics education experts, which operationalizes problem-solving as four stages and eight diagnostic sub-skills. By specifying what evidence to elicit and assess at each stage, STEP enables an LLM pipeline to generate stage-specific questions and rubrics for any math word problem, reducing the manual design of diagnostic materials. An expert review (N=8) assessed the pedagogical validity of the generated materials and informed STEPwise, a teacher-in-the-loop system for diagnostic material generation and process-level assessment. In a classroom study with 5 teachers and 64 students, STEPwise helped teachers and students locate reasoning breakdowns and supported students in reflecting on their reasoning. Together, STEP and STEPwise offer a structured approach to fine-grained diagnosis at classroom scale.

papers.title: BehaviorFormer: Discovering Behavioral Patterns via Clusterable Next-Token Prediction
papers.abstract: Discovering behavioral patterns in open-ended games is challenging due to the lack of clear objectives or ground-truth annotations. In this work, we extend a next-token prediction Transformer with the deep clustering algorithm DCSS to learn meaningful representations with well-separated clusters. In a controlled Minecraft session with 26 players, the method discovers 23 distinct behavioral patterns that generalize across the studied players, further refining structures present in self-supervised representations into clearly separable clusters. We group the clusters into seven interpretable categories covering stationary, roaming, travel, mining, base work, logging, and farming behavior.

papers.title: FlowAvatar: Real-Time Full-Body Avatars from Sparse Egocentric Inputs on Consumer XR Devices
papers.abstract: Prior avatar embodiment research has studied tracking completeness (how faithfully the body, hands, and face are sensed and reproduced) and personalized appearance in isolation, each requiring specialized lab equipment. How these factors interact on consumer hardware remains an open question, because no existing system unifies body pose, face, hands, and personalized appearance on a standalone headset. We present FlowAvatar, a system enabling real-time personalized look-alike avatars with full-body pose, hand articulation, facial expression, and eye gaze tracking from sparse egocentric inputs on consumer XR devices (Meta Quest Pro). Our pose model achieves competitive spatial accuracy and state-of-the-art temporal consistency on the AMASS benchmark against prior works with comprehensive spatial and temporal losses validated through architecture and loss ablations, while running in real-time. Two user studies (N=12, N=10) provide converging evidence that tracking completeness and personalized appearance serve complementary roles: tracking completeness broadly improves perceived motion quality, while only their combination achieves positive total embodiment.

papers.title: {Access|Use|Sustain|_}-ability: Exploration and Quantification of a Linguistic Structure and Its Use in HCI
papers.abstract: Language plays a crucial role in research and technology design, throughout problem formulation, method descriptions, analysis of findings, and interpretation. In this paper, we focus on a particular, trending linguistic pattern in the Human-Computer Interaction literature, which we call -abilities. Examples include usability, accessibility, and explainability. These -abilities have become increasingly popular, with potential impacts on the discipline. They take a verb, turn it into an adjective, and finally nominalize it. We approach the -abilities phenomenon with a survey of the HCI literature between 1988 and 2025. All in all, we identified 349 different -abilities. Moreover, the use of -abilities notably increased since the late 2000s, both in the absolute number of different -abilities and the frequency of use of the most popular ones. The majority of -abilities we found had a positive notion, and most -abilities with a negative notion are prefixed counterparts of their positive opposite (e.g., un+sustainability). We critically discuss implications of their increased use. First, -abilities change the literal meaning of design intentions. For example, acceptability reduces the concrete verb accepting into only its potential (acceptable), and finally nominalizes it, claiming the existence of acceptability as a somewhat stable and real, abstract characteristic of a technology. Second, the prefix-based opposite construction can weaken the design goal. Un+sustainability avoids clarification of the -ability's meaning (here e.g., ecological or financial), and does not spell out the expected impact of designs that are not sustainable (e.g., the destruction of nature). Future work should compare the use of -abilities in English with other languages to better understand the ways in which they transform meaning.

papers.title: Exploring Mixed Reality for Engagement in Robotics: A Comparison of Robot Control Methods
papers.abstract: This paper presents a Mixed Reality (MR) robotics experience that provides an accessible introduction to interacting with a physical robot. The application combines a TurtleBot with a virtual animal-tending activity and three control methods: Joystick, Waypoint, and Path-Drawing. A mixed-methods user study with 10 participants investigated changes in robotics interest and confidence following the experience and how the control methods influenced engagement, workload, and preference. Confidence increased following the experience, with the exploratory analysis indicating a significant pre--post difference, while the increase in interest was not statistically significant. The control methods produced clear differences in perceived workload and ease of use, with Path-Drawing generally more demanding and difficult to use. Joystick was preferred by eight of ten participants and was associated with better perceived performance and lower frustration. However, no statistically significant differences were detected in the other engagement dimensions, suggesting that the most preferred method was not necessarily more engaging across all aspects of the experience. These findings highlight the importance of considering both usability and engagement when designing how users interact with robots in introductory MR experiences.

papers.title: GUIDE: Computationally Augmented Consensus for Trustworthy Clinical Practice Guidelines
papers.abstract: Maintaining up-to-date clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) is essential for evidence-based medicine, but rapid evidence growth and complex expert consensus formation limit timely updates. We developed GUIDE, a multi-agent copilot system for human-AI collaborative guideline generation and updating. GUIDE delegates labor-intensive tasks to specialized AI agents while preserving expert judgment and final arbitration. In 12 NICE ophthalmology datasets, GUIDE achieved 88.85% literature recall, 86.06% alignment in certainty-of-evidence ratings, and 91.67% recommendation agreement, requiring 162.17 minutes per dataset on average (28.68% human intervention). Performance remained stable across 20 additional datasets from cardiology, endocrinology, gastroenterology, and respiratory medicine. Ablation analysis showed that removing expert intervention reduced performance in judgment-intensive steps such as Risk-of-Bias assessment. In six post-cutoff datasets, GUIDE maintained robust end-to-end performance on unseen evidence. Prospective real-world validation showed that GUIDE reduced expert workload and produced more clinically acceptable recommendations than the original decade-old guideline (mean score, 3.73 vs. 1.53; agreement, 66.7% vs. 13.3%), with outcomes comparable to human-only updating (P = 0.588) but substantially less time and effort. GUIDE offers a practical framework for timely, trustworthy, expert-centric guideline development and validates computationally augmented consensus.

papers.title: A Mechanomyography-Based Integrated Sensing-Stimulation System for Fatigue-Aware Neuromuscular Therapy
papers.abstract: Muscle fatigue limits the effectiveness of functional electrical stimulation (FES), yet fatigue monitoring during active stimulation remains challenging because electromyography (EMG) is severely contaminated by stimulation artifacts. To address this issue, this study proposes an integrated mechanomyography-based sensing framework (MMG-FES) for artifact-resistant fatigue monitoring during stimulation. Fatigue states were first characterized during voluntary movement using established EMG spectral indicators, including median frequency (MF) and mean power frequency (MPF), and then linked to MMG-derived features, including high-frequency energy ratio (HFER) and spectral bandwidth (BW), for fatigue recognition under stimulation conditions. Experimental results showed consistent fatigue-related trends, with EMG spectral features decreasing and MMG features exhibiting coordinated spectral redistribution across repeated contractions. Using these features, the proposed framework achieved fatigue-state recognition accuracies of 0.93 and 0.96 with logistic regression and random forest, respectively. These findings support MMG as a physiologically meaningful and stimulation-compatible modality for fatigue-aware closed-loop neuromuscular stimulation.

papers.title: Vision: "What Don't I Know About User's Preferences?" How Uncertainty Estimation Improves Proactive Assistant Alignment
papers.abstract: Proactive Smart Assistants (PSAs) increasingly use general knowledge, learned patterns from group-level data, patterns from individual user's data, and recent sensor observations to anticipate which action a user may prefer. Existing systems typically select actions from predicted user preference likelihoods, but these likelihoods alone do not reveal how reliable the prediction is, which evidence supports it, or why ambiguity remains. In this vision paper, we argue that uncertainty estimation can provide this missing information and substantially change appropriate downstream behavior. Using the example of a home assistant, we introduce the questions that uncertainty estimation aims to answer, i.e. how sure is the assistant about the predicted preference likelihood, whether the confidence come from group-level assumptions or individual's data, and whether likelihood ambiguity reflect the user's intrinsic preference variability or insufficient data for the particular situation. We further introduce uncertainty estimation applications in neighboring domains, such as human trajectory prediction, personalized activity recognition, information-collection, and model-based control. Finally, we draw on insights from neighboring domains to envision how future uncertainty-aware proactive assistants may address key challenges in proactive interaction.

papers.title: FreeBrush: Motor Signals-Based Toothbrushing Monitoring System for Electric Toothbrushes
papers.abstract: Oral health is vital for overall well-being, yet many users brush different tooth surfaces for insufficient or excessive durations. Toothbrushing monitoring systems can help improve brushing habits by reminding users of under-brushed and over-brushed surfaces, but existing approaches often rely on external sensors, increasing cost and reducing practicality. We observe that the intrinsic motor signals of electric toothbrushes can reflect the brushing surfaces and durations. When brushing different tooth surfaces, the brush head experiences different constraints from the surrounding oral cavity, changing the motor's driving currents and position feedback. Based on this observation, we propose FreeBrush, a toothbrushing monitoring system that uses the intrinsic motor signals of electric toothbrushes to recognize brushed tooth surfaces and estimate brushing durations without any external sensors. We prototype the system on a commercial off-the-shelf electric toothbrush and conduct a comprehensive evaluation with 18 participants. FreeBrush achieves 92.8% accuracy for 16-surface recognition and 92.0% accuracy for brushing duration estimation. The system further shows robustness across different toothpastes, brush heads, vibration modes, usage scenarios, and long-term use, and is capable of running on edge devices. By recognizing brushed tooth surfaces and estimating the brushing duration, FreeBrush can help users identify under-brushed and over-brushed surfaces and build balanced brushing habits.

papers.title: A Co-Located MMG-FES Wearable Interface for Action-Updated State-Gated Stimulation
papers.abstract: Functional electrical stimulation (FES) assists movement, but fixed schedules cannot track how a repeatedly activated muscle changes, and surface electromyography (EMG) near the stimulation electrodes is often obscured by artifacts. Prior work recorded mechanomyography (MMG) passively during closed-loop FES cycling and estimated FES-induced fatigue or predicted fatigue for FES control, without gating stimulation with stimulated-site MMG. In this study, we present VG-FES, a wearable module co-locating microphone-based MMG, programmable charge-balanced biphasic stimulation, and embedded state-gated control at one on-skin thigh site. After each action, we compare rectus femoris (RF) mean power frequency (MPF) with an early-session baseline of the same direction, giving a relative state. A threshold on its window means enables fixed-duration bursts separated by rest periods. During onboard stimulation, MMG remained recordable, whereas near-site EMG was artifact-dominated. Under prolonged external stimulation, cycle-wise MMG tracked an independent local-pressure reference (Spearman rho = 0.968). In leave-one-session-out evaluation on 2284 squat actions (11 sessions, eight participants), MMG-based action segmentation reached an event-detection F1 of 0.923 and direction classification a balanced accuracy of 0.925. Online, over 15.69 min of self-paced squats, one participant received four bursts while MMG acquisition and action monitoring continued. Mechanical feedback from the stimulated site offers wearable FES and assistive robotics a per-action basis for state-gated stimulation.

papers.title: Side-Vent Design for Microphone-Based Mechanomyography Sensors: Modeling and Experimental Evaluation of Contact Dependence
papers.abstract: Wearable muscle sensing for rehabilitation, assistive robotics, and electrical-stimulation feedback needs mechanomyography sensors less sensitive to fit changes during wear. In microphone-based mechanomyography, cavity pressure depends on rim contact, a dependence housing design has rarely targeted. This study evaluates a side-vented housing, whose vent opens a pressure-relief path in parallel with the rim to lower contact dependence, and quantifies the acoustic-gain cost. Thermoviscous finite-element simulations compared twenty cavity configurations under prescribed source motion. Paired bench sweeps over 10-200 Hz on both housings compared direct contact with a Gap-ring spacer, a radially grooved spacer ring. At 100 Hz, side venting reduced the simulated acoustic-gain variation across 0.10-0.50 mm rim clearances from 25.8 to 10.0 dB and cost 5.5 dB of gain at 0.20 mm clearance. Velocity fields and branch-flow calculations identified this path. At the higher speaker drive level, the Gap-ring spacer caused median attenuations of 13.6 dB (vented) and 30.1 dB (unvented) relative to direct contact. In this front end, a 35.9-dB signal-gain increase at 100 Hz raised the calculated operational-amplifier voltage-noise gain by 1.6 dB. A single-participant demonstration of paced elbow flexion and extension compared envelope timing and spectra between housings, finding similar envelope timing (correlation 0.935) and broadly similar spectra (correlation 0.956). Vent area trades acoustic gain against contact dependence and can therefore serve as a housing design parameter.

papers.title: AuthScribe: Supporting Agency and Authorship in LLM-Assisted Reflective Journaling
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used in reflective journaling, where articulating an experience is part of interpreting it. This raises questions about how writers retain authorship, exercise agency, and assess personalized assistance. We present AuthScribe, an LLM-assisted reflective journaling system that combines contextual anchors, writer-steered AI support, Autobiographical Citations, and read-only Provisional Drafts that require re-expression before AI-generated suggestions enter the journal. Retrieval and LLM inference run on-device. In a 14-day field deployment with 14 participants, grounding shifted from situating current experiences to reconnecting them with prior self-authored interpretations. Perceived agency remained stable through Week 1 and shifted during Week 2. Participants described authorship through transforming AI-generated suggestions into personally meaningful expression, and trusted personalized prompts when they could trace them to prior writing. We discuss design implications for adoption friction, longitudinal agency, and traceable personalization in AI systems for personal reflection.

papers.title: ArguScale: Evidence-Grounded Human-AI Sensemaking Across Concurrent Live Conversations
papers.abstract: Monitoring concurrent classroom collaborative reasoning discussions is challenging because instructors have to track collaboration-relevant behaviors across multiple ongoing conversations at once. Existing Human-AI conversational sensemaking systems can scale monitoring upward through summaries and visual abstractions, but these representations may distance users from underlying conversational evidence, e.g., relevant audio and transcript segments, needed to forage downward. Through our formative study, we developed ArguScale, an evidence-grounded Human-AI sensemaking system that organizes interactional signals into temporally aligned representations linked to transcript and audio evidence. A temporal signal-density view provides temporal context and supports rapid cross-group comparison, while selective evidence access allows instructors to inspect audio and transcript. We evaluated ArguScale in a mixed-design study with 20 participants. Compared to other conditions, ArguScale improved participants' ability to efficiently and accurately identify collaboration-relevant cues. We further identify strategies participants used to forage for and make sense of conversational evidence under live time constraints.

papers.title: NUISS: A User-Centered Prototype for International Student Administrative Support
papers.abstract: This study applies a streamlined User-Centered Design (UCD) approach, enhanced with AI elements, to address common administrative challenges faced by international students, such as information fragmentation and unclear processes. Using National University (NU) as a case study, the research followed core UCD stages to develop the prototype of the NU International Student Services (NUISS). These stages included task analysis informed by user stories, persona development, prototype design, and a heuristic evaluation. The high-fidelity prototype integrates three key modules-Visa Services, Certification, and Paymentwith an AI-powered assistant for proactive, personalized support. The structure is designed to enhance accessibility and minimize cognitive load. An evaluation that centered on "consistency and standards" uncovered major interface problems; this led to design refinements that boosted visual clarity and balance in a significant way. The final prototype shows that applying UCD principles in a focused way, combined with AI enhancements, can create efficient and user-friendly administrative experiences, and it offers a replicable model for similar educational contexts.

papers.title: From Embedded Finance to Embedded Obligation: A Law-and-Economics Theory of Consumer Protection in Platform-Mediated Financial Services
papers.abstract: Embedded finance is usually described as the integration of financial services into non-financial platforms. This article argues that the deeper regulatory transformation is the embedding of future legal and economic obligations into ordinary consumption, work, business, and entertainment environments. When credit, payment, wage-advance, wallet, and merchant-financing functions are delivered through plat form architecture, consumer protection cannot focus only on the formal product or licensed provider. It must also examine how obligations are framed, made salient or obscure, personalized through data, and allocated across platforms, merchants, lenders, and technical intermediaries. The article develops a law and-economics theory of Embedded Obligation Architecture, explains its irreducible object, refines its four layers, and distinguishes it from choice architecture, digital nudging, dark patterns, behavioral contract theory, and platform governance. It specifies the evidentiary limits of transferring behavioral evidence to embedded-finance contexts and proposes a Functional Embedded Obligation Test as a standard with gateway elements, evidentiary thresholds, legal vehicles, safe harbors, and proportionate remedies.

papers.title: The Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Korean Language Learning: Applications, Challenges, and Instructional Strategies
papers.abstract: This conceptual narrative review examines the role of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in Korean language learning. The paper synthesizes recent scholarship on AI-assisted language learning, Korean language education, technology acceptance, and educational ethics to develop an analytical framework for responsible classroom use. The review focuses on four dimensions: Korean language skills, Korean-specific linguistic and cultural features, instructional design, and governance risks. The analysis suggests that generative AI can support listening, speaking, reading, and writing when tasks are explicitly designed around Korean phonology, morphology, pragmatics, and learner purposes such as TOPIK preparation, study abroad, employment, and popular-culture engagement. It also identifies challenges in cultural-pragmatic accuracy, hallucinated expressions, assessment validity, data privacy, unequal access, teacher readiness, and learner dependency. The paper concludes that generative AI should function as a mediated learning resource rather than a substitute for teachers, learner judgment, or culturally grounded interaction.

papers.title: Research on Attention Guidance and User Autonomy in AI-Powered Immersive Environments
papers.abstract: As artificial intelligence gets deeply embedded into immersive environments, attention-guiding technology delivers ever more precise and efficient outcomes. Still, this improved efficiency carries an overlooked design risk: excessive AI guidance may steadily erode user agency and undermine exploratory behaviors as well as the process of meaning-making. This paper builds a critical conceptual framework to rethink attention-oriented design within AI-driven immersive settings. It defines excessive guidance and establishes theoretical links between this concept and three core facets of user agency: perceived control, voluntary choice and decision-making authority. Based on these findings, the paper calls for a paradigm shift from attention optimization to curiosity-led design. It also puts forward actionable behavioral measurement indicators covering exploration scope, average dwell time, path-following ratio, active choice frequency and recall test performance. The proposed framework supplies a new theoretical tool for human-computer interaction research in immersive scenarios and helps shift AI's role from a fixed route provider to an exploratory collaborator.

papers.title: A Study on the Mechanism and Ways to Improve New-Quality Productivity of Enterprises Driven by AI and the Digital Economy
papers.abstract: With the deep development of the digital economy and the accelerated iteration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, the formation and development of enterprise new quality productive forces have attracted increasing attention from academia and practice. Based on enterprises as the micro-subject, this paper constructs a theoretical analysis framework for the "dual-wheel drive of AI and the digital economy" and explores the formation mechanism and the path to enhancing the synergistic empowerment of enterprise these forces. The research finds that AI and the digital economy are not simply parallel drivers, but form a synergistic empowerment effect through a triple interactive mechanism of "technology-factor-organization." AI technology reshapes the technological boundary of the production function, while the digital economy reconstructs the allocation logic of production factors. The deep integration of the two drives a fundamental transformation of enterprise production modes from "factor-input-driven" to "innovation-driven". On this basis, this paper reveals the formation mechanism of these advanced productive capabilities across three dimensions: technological innovation, data element allocation, and organizational change, and proposes corresponding enhancement paths. This study has significant theoretical and practical value for understanding the micro-formation mechanism of enterprise new-quality productive forces and for guiding enterprise digital transformation and intelligent upgrading.

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.abstract: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Measuring Activity-Space Segregation with Multi-Source Big Data: A Physical--Digital Framework with Simulation Validation and a Real-Data Proof of Concept
papers.abstract: Segregation research increasingly measures who people encounter beyond home, yet physical mobility, place semantics, and digital activity are often combined without clear construct boundaries. This study develops a physical--digital activity-space framework that distinguishes co-presence, digital exposure, and digital interaction, and represents physical and digital segregation as separate components rather than a forced composite. Validation is deliberately split by evidentiary role. A public Washington--Baltimore Foursquare check-in subset tests the computational feasibility and robustness of a discrete group co-visitation statistic; it does not validate continuous socioeconomic exposure because the dataset lacks individual socioeconomic status. Monte Carlo experiments separately test layer-selective construct response and sensitivity to trace missingness, spatial aggregation, socioeconomic measurement error, and cross-layer coupling. The results show that the proposed calculations are executable and that the synthetic physical and digital components respond selectively to their generating mechanisms, while also revealing important measurement attenuation. No real-data estimate of income segregation, digital exposure, physical--digital coupling, or the causal effect of inequality is reported. The framework therefore combines bounded validation with a falsifiable comparative and causal research agenda.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.abstract: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.abstract: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent games and serious real-world aggression remains more contested, with recent research emphasizing relatively small effects and the importance of individual and contextual factors. Overall, the evidence suggests that the developmental consequences of gaming for children and adolescents depend less on gaming itself than on the duration, content, context, and pattern of engagement.

papers.title: Designing an Artificial Intelligence–Based Cognitive Empowerment Package to Enhance Entrepreneurial Skills in Gifted and Creative Adolescents
papers.abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to design an artificial intelligence–based cognitive empowerment package for enhancing entrepreneurial skills in gifted and creative adolescents through the qualitative identification and integration of relevant cognitive, psychological, motivational, interpersonal, and technological components. Methods and Materials: The study employed a qualitative exploratory-developmental design. Data were obtained through an analytical review of relevant literature, examination of previous student entrepreneurship workshop experiences, and semi-structured interviews with students, mentors, workshop facilitators, and accelerator managers selected through purposive sampling. Data collection continued until conceptual saturation was achieved. Interview transcripts, field observations, documentary evidence, and analytical notes were examined using thematic analysis. Findings: The qualitative analysis indicated that sustained entrepreneurial action among gifted and creative adolescents depends on a multidimensional configuration of entrepreneurial intention and identity, self-efficacy, opportunity recognition and problem identification, executive functioning, tolerance of ambiguity, applied creativity, fear of failure and perfectionism, intrinsic motivation and psychological ownership, teamwork and psychological safety, proactive agency, resilience, future orientation, and reflective readiness to use artificial intelligence. The findings further suggested that entrepreneurial difficulties differ across adolescents and therefore require profile-based rather than uniform intervention. Integration of the themes resulted in a six-session package encompassing profile awareness and goal setting, problem identification and value creation, conversion of ideas into action plans, presentation and feedback utilization, teamwork and agency, and final presentation with a continuation plan. Conclusion: The findings suggest that entrepreneurial empowerment in gifted and creative adolescents should extend beyond creativity and business knowledge by strengthening the cognitive and psychological capacities required to transform ideas into sustained action, while using artificial intelligence as a supervised reflective and personalized learning support rather than as a substitute for adolescent judgment and agency.

papers.title: The Effect of Artificial Intelligence–Induced Stress on Employees’ Individual Creativity: Examining the Roles of Stress-Coping Strategies and Management Commitment
papers.abstract: Objective: The present study aimed to investigate the effect of artificial intelligence–induced stress on employees’ individual creativity, considering the mediating role of stress-coping strategies and the moderating role of management commitment. Methods and Materials: In terms of purpose, this was an applied study, and methodologically, it employed a descriptive survey design. The statistical population comprised all permanent employees of the Yazd City Gas Company between September 2025 and March 2026. Based on Cochran’s formula, 125 employees were selected through simple random sampling. Data were collected using the standardized questionnaire developed by Tong et al. (2025), which assessed artificial intelligence–induced stress, stress-coping strategies, individual creativity, and management commitment. The validity of the instrument was confirmed through confirmatory factor analysis, average variance extracted, and the Fornell–Larcker criterion, while its reliability was verified using Cronbach’s alpha and composite reliability. The data were analyzed using SPSS version 26 and structural equation modeling in SmartPLS version 4. Findings: The results indicated that artificial intelligence–induced stress had a direct and significant effect on stress-coping strategies, which, in turn, significantly enhanced employees’ individual creativity. The indirect effect of artificial intelligence–induced stress on individual creativity through the mediating variable of stress-coping strategies was also confirmed. However, the direct effect of artificial intelligence–induced stress on individual creativity was not statistically significant. Furthermore, the moderating role of management commitment in the relationship between artificial intelligence–induced stress and stress-coping strategies was not confirmed. Conclusion: The findings demonstrated that artificial intelligence–induced stress does not necessarily lead directly to a reduction in employee creativity; rather, the manner in which employees manage and cope with this stress determines its creative outcomes. The use of adaptive coping strategies can transform technology-related pressures into opportunities for learning, intrinsic motivation, and creative ideation.

papers.title: Designing a Model for Enhancing the Skills of Primary School Principals with an Emphasis on STEAM Education
papers.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to design a comprehensive model for enhancing the professional and managerial skills of primary school principals with an emphasis on the implementation of Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics (STEAM) education. Methods and Materials: This qualitative study employed a thematic analysis design. The study population consisted of primary school principals, experts in school management and STEAM education, university faculty members, educational administrators, and specialists working in the 22 education districts of Tehran, Iran. Fifteen participants were selected through purposive sampling, and recruitment continued until theoretical data saturation was achieved. Data were collected through in-depth, semi-structured interviews designed to explore participants’ experiences, perceptions, and recommendations regarding the competencies required by primary school principals for the successful implementation of STEAM education. The interview data were transcribed, coded, categorized, and analyzed using thematic network analysis. The credibility and consistency of the findings were supported through systematic coding, continuous comparison of the extracted concepts, expert review, and revision of the thematic structure. Findings: The thematic network analysis identified 155 initial codes, which were classified into 28 organizing themes and six global themes. The six principal dimensions of the proposed model were strategic and transformational leadership of primary school principals in implementing STEAM education; development of the professional and managerial competencies of school human resources; establishment of a participatory, innovative, and learning-oriented organizational culture; management of resources, processes, and the quality of STEAM program implementation; enhancement of managerial communication, collaboration, and networking skills; and sustainability, alignment, institutionalization, and inclusive implementation of STEAM programs in primary schools. These interconnected dimensions constituted the main structural components of the proposed skill-enhancement model. Conclusion: The proposed model indicates that successful STEAM implementation requires primary school principals to possess integrated leadership, professional, communicative, organizational, and resource-management competencies.

papers.title: An Investigation of Management Practices in Raw Material Cost Accounting: Evidence from Iraqi Industrial Companies
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate management practices in raw material cost accounting and their effects on cost control and optimization in Iraqi industrial companies. In terms of purpose, the study was applied, and in terms of nature, it employed a descriptive-correlational survey design. The statistical population consisted of financial managers, cost accountants, and cost-control specialists working in Iraqi industrial companies. Using Cochran’s formula, the sample size was determined to be 384 participants, who were selected through stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a researcher-developed questionnaire comprising 25 items rated on a five-point Likert scale. Descriptive statistics, Spearman’s rank-order correlation test, and multiple linear regression analysis were performed using SPSS software. The results showed that raw material cost-management challenges had the highest mean score of 4.10 out of 5, whereas raw material inventory and consumption management had the lowest mean score of 3.25. The most important challenges were severe fluctuations in raw material prices and supply chain disruptions. The hypothesis-testing results also indicated that cost-management practices (β = 0.34) and inventory management (β = 0.29) had positive and statistically significant effects on cost control, whereas cost-management challenges (β = −0.22) had a negative and statistically significant effect. The regression model explained 52.4% of the variance in the dependent variable. Iraqi industrial companies face serious challenges in managing raw material costs, primarily arising from external factors, including price fluctuations and supply chain disruptions, as well as internal weaknesses, such as inadequate information systems and traditional inventory-management practices. Strengthening cost-management practices and improving inventory management can contribute substantially to reducing costs and increasing the profitability of these companies.

papers.title: The Voice of AI: Consumer Psychology and the Strategic Use of AI-Generated Voices in Marketing
papers.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence is transforming marketing communication, with AI-generated voices emerging as an increasingly important means through which brands communicate with consumers. This paper examines AI-generated voices from a consumer psychology perspective, focusing on how consumers interpret and respond to synthetic voices used in marketing communication. Drawing on literature from artificial intelligence, marketing, consumer behaviour and human–computer interaction, the paper explores the psychological significance of vocal characteristics such as naturalness, human-likeness, prosody, anthropomorphism and emotional expression. It further examines how these characteristics can shape consumer perceptions of message credibility, authenticity and brand trust. The discussion highlights the growing use of AI-generated voices across advertising, social media, voice commerce and interactive brand communication, with selected examples from the Indian marketing context illustrating their applications in personalisation, engagement and localisation. The paper argues that the effectiveness of AI-generated voices depends not simply on technological sophistication, but on how consumers psychologically interpret the voice and its relationship with the message and brand. The paper concludes by identifying directions for future research on AI-mediated brand communication.

papers.title: Neuromorphic Computing Architectures for Low-Power Edge Inference in IoT Applications
papers.abstract: The blistering advancements witnessed in the Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem have led to the urgency of search outcomes that provide energy efficient, low latency, and smart processing support that manifests itself right at the edge. The traditional edge computing devices built on von Neumann architecture are inherently limited by being optimized to be adjacent in memory and processing components, which results in the high power required and latency, which are highly undesirable in devices with limited power resources; wearables, smart sensors, and remote-monitoring systems. A Neuromorphic computing approach based on the human brain blueprint presents a better alternative due to its implementation of spiking neural networks (SNNs) that allow asynchronous and event-driven computation, thus dramatically lowering power demand and yet being able to run real-time inference. This paper includes a holistic comparison of the most recent examples of the neuromorphic hardware platforms, such as Intel Loihi, IBM TrueNorth, and BrainScaleS system, with regard to their learning architectures, energy consumption, throughput, and suitability to the edge-based IoT applications. An empirical case study is carried out, which is a keyword spotting case study and event-based gesture recognition case study using Google Speech Commands and the DVS Gesture dataset sets, respectively. The neuromorphic systems presented a significant energy per inference improvement up to 15x and reduced latency at about 30 on traditional ARM Cortex-M7-based ANN implementations at very slight sacrifices in terms of classification accuracy. In addition, the Loihi platform showed on-chip learning utilizing spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), which made the platform capable of dynamic and adaptive inference in fluctuating IoT applications. This paper also examines the integration issues of neuromorphic systems which include the compatibility with sensor modalities, immature software toolchains, and complexities to convert ANN to SNN. The results indicate that neuromorphic systems are highly suitable in ultra-low-power edge intelligence and provide a paradigm of scalable and biologically inspired, next-generation IoT systems. The lines of future research are described in such aspects as hybrid neuromorphic edge-cloud learning, unification of benchmark requirements, and designing secure, programmable, and reconfigurable neuromorphic co-processors to support adaptive edge AI.

papers.title: Empowerment of Islamic Religious Education Teachers through Generative AI Training for the Development of Islamic Value-Based Learning Media at SMP Negeri 35 Medan
papers.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, particularly Generative AI, has created new opportunities for developing innovative, interactive, and contextual learning media. However, many Islamic Religious Education (IRE) teachers still have limited competencies in utilizing this technology as a learning medium while maintaining Islamic values. This Community Service Program (PKM) aimed to improve the competence of IRE teachers at SMP Negeri 35 Medan in utilizing Generative AI to develop creative, effective, and Islamic value-based learning media. The program employed a Participatory Action Learning approach consisting of needs identification, educational sessions, practical training, mentoring, and evaluation. The training involved demonstrations and hands-on practice using various Generative AI platforms, including ChatGPT, Canva AI, Gamma AI, and Microsoft Copilot, to develop teaching materials, presentations, assessment questions, and visual learning media based on Islamic values. The results indicated an improvement in participants' understanding of Generative AI, enhanced skills in developing digital learning media, and increased awareness of the ethical use of AI from an Islamic perspective. The teachers were able to produce learning media that were more engaging, interactive, contextual, and supportive of the implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum. This program contributed positively to improving teachers' digital literacy while strengthening the integration of technology and Islamic values in the IRE learning process.

papers.title: FROM INFLUENCE TO INTENT: SYSTEMATICALLY REVIEWING THE ROLE OF SOCIAL MEDIA INFLUENCERS IN PURCHASING BEHAVIOUR
papers.abstract: Background: In the digital moving age, social media influencers (SMIs) have emerged as strong agents altering consumer behaviour and hence, there was a need to conduct systematic literature analysis present on social media influencers.Objectives: Broadly, to explore the impact of social media influencers on consumer purchase behaviour.Methods: This systematic literature review explores the impact of social media influencers on consumer purchase behaviour, synthesizing findings from academic research published over the period of 15 years (2011 to 2025). PRISMA is being used as the methodology for conducting this literature review.Results: The review identifies key factors such as influencer credibility, authenticity, engagement, content quality, and platform characteristics that prominently influence consumer trust and By employing, simultaneously, their buying behaviour.Conclusion: Social media influencers significantly impact consumer trust and buying behaviour. The review categorizes the literature into thematic clusters, including influencer marketing strategies and consumer psychology.

papers.title: Cyber Soldier project - A threat-led methodology for assessing the Digital Resilience of cybersecurity systems
papers.abstract: In order to comply with European regulatory frameworks like the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), we propose the Cyber Soldier approach and tool set, which presents a threat-led approach for evaluating the digital resilience of cybersecurity systems inside enterprises. This approach, in contrast to conventional vulnerability assessments or penetration testing, focuses on simulating the tactics, methods, and procedures (TTPs) of actual attackers in order to assess the efficacy of operational resilience mechanisms and cybersecurity measures in production systems. In order to assess the organization's readiness for complex cyberthreats, the suggested approach combines threat information, red team scenario creation, and detection performance analysis into a single procedure. We show how the proposed framework connects the operational practice of resilience testing with the strategic compliance obligations under DORA. We also provide some preliminary statistics about the use of the Cyber Soldier toolkit in practical settings.

papers.title: PENINGKATAN KESADARAN PELAJAR TERHADAP PENGGUNAAN SMARTPHONE, MEDIA SOSIAL, DAN KEAMANAN DIGITAL
papers.abstract: Perkembangan teknologi digital menjadikan smartphone dan media sosial sebagai bagian penting dalam kehidupan pelajar, tetapi penggunaannya juga menghadirkan berbagai risiko, seperti pelanggaran privasi, cyberbullying, phishing, penyebaran informasi yang tidak benar, dan penggunaan secara berlebihan. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan memperkuat kesadaran pelajar mengenai penggunaan smartphone dan media sosial secara aman, sehat, etis, dan bertanggung jawab. Kegiatan dilaksanakan kepada 175 pelajar kelas XII, terdiri atas 120 pelajar SMA Negeri 1 Aek Kuasan dan 55 pelajar SMK YASPENDA Pulau Rakyat. Metode yang digunakan adalah pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif melalui penyampaian materi secara langsung menggunakan presentasi, interaksi dan pertanyaan sederhana, observasi respons peserta, dokumentasi, serta evaluasi internal. Materi meliputi manfaat smartphone dan media sosial, ancaman digital, perlindungan data pribadi, cyberbullying, phishing, penipuan daring, verifikasi informasi, etika bermedia sosial, privasi, jejak digital, dan penggunaan smartphone secara bijak. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa pelajar mengikuti kegiatan dengan antusias, aktif merespons materi dan pertanyaan, serta menunjukkan pemahaman berdasarkan pengamatan selama kegiatan. Namun, karena tidak dilakukan pre-test dan post-test, perubahan tingkat kesadaran digital belum dapat diukur secara statistik. Kegiatan ini menunjukkan pentingnya edukasi digital yang dilakukan secara berkelanjutan di lingkungan sekolah.

papers.title: Competition and Diversity in Generative AI
papers.abstract: Recent evidence, both in the laboratory and in the wild, suggests that the use of generative artificial intelligence reduces the diversity of content produced. As generative AI penetrates more markets and reaches widespread adoption, should we still expect to see content homogenization? Our work begins with a simple observation: content producers do not act in isolation. Instead, they compete with one another (e.g., for customers or attention). We explore the impact competition has on both content diversity and overall social welfare when producers use generative AI. Through a formal game-theoretic model, we show that competitive markets select for diverse AI models, mitigating monoculture. We further show that a generative AI model that performs well in isolation (i.e., according to a benchmark) may fail to provide value in a competitive market. Our results highlight the importance of evaluating generative AI models across the breadth of their output distributions, particularly when they will be deployed in competitive environments. We validate our theoretical results with a series of experiments involving generative text and image models. Overall, our results suggest that homogenization due to generative AI is unlikely to persist under strong competition. This paper was accepted by Itai Ashlagi, market design, platform, and demand analytics. papers.title: Data Optimization for LLMs: A Survey
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have attracted great attention in both academic and industrial communities in recent years. Numerous survey studies have covered various aspects of LLMs, such as learning strategies, applications, alignment, explainability, and evaluation. However, little headway has been made in reviewing data-related aspects for LLMs, despite data being recognized as a key factor contributing to the emergence of the LLMs era. A wide range of data optimization algorithms and techniques are employed in LLMs' training and application processes. These techniques often originate from diverse deep learning domains, with their theoretical inspirations and heuristic motivations appearing unrelated to each other. This study aims to develop a comprehensive framework for LLMs' data optimization techniques to enhance data utilization efficiency. We first discuss data challenges in LLMs' training and inference. Second, we summarize data perception dimensions for evaluating LLMs' data properties. Third, existing optimization techniques are reviewed and categorized into four groups: data selection, augmentation, reweighting, and others. Fourth, we analyze interconnections between these categories. Finally, we identify key challenges and future directions for LLMs' data optimization compared with conventional deep learning approaches.

papers.title: Study buddy learning is associated with academic success in undergraduate science courses
papers.abstract: for undergraduate science students. The study tested three hypotheses: (i) Do students benefit academically from a formalized study buddy peer learning program? (ii) Do mentors and protégés benefit equally from participation in the study buddy program? (iii) Does heterogeneity in group members' initial academic performance have an effect on benefits from participation in the study buddy program? To test these hypotheses, we implemented a cohort-based study buddy program in which high-scoring students (mentors) and lower-scoring peers (protégés), following their first assessment scores in a given course, were invited to form study groups. We compared the performance of participants versus non-participants on subsequent assessments, while examining separately the effects for mentors and protégés. Results showed (i) significant grade benefits for participants over non-participants, (ii) similar participation benefits for students in mentor and protégé roles, and (iii) no interaction of competence-based heterogeneity on these effects. Although this study design was unable to assess the nature of the study buddy interactions, the grade performance data highlight the program as a cost-effective and scalable approach to enhance students' educational experiences. The data also emphasize the value of reducing barriers to collaborative learning in higher education.

papers.title: Encoding tactile stimuli for Braille recognition with organoids
papers.abstract: This study proposes a transferable encoding strategy that maps tactile sensor data to electrical stimulation patterns, enabling neural organoids to perform an open-loop artificial tactile Braille classification task. Human forebrain organoids cultured on a low-density microelectrode array (MEA) are systematically stimulated to characterize the relationship between electrical stimulation parameters (number of pulse, phase amplitude, phase duration, and trigger delay) and organoid responses, measured as spike activity and spatial displacement of the center of activity. Implemented on event-based tactile inputs recorded from the Evetac sensor, our system achieved an average Braille letter classification accuracy of 61% with a single organoid, which increased to 83% when responses from a three-organoid ensemble were combined. Additionally, the multi-organoid configuration demonstrated enhanced robustness against various types of artificially introduced noise. This research demonstrates the potential of organoids as low-power, adaptive bio-hybrid computational elements and provides a foundational encoding framework for future scalable bio-hybrid computing architectures.

papers.title: Cloud‐Native and Distributed Systems for Efficient and Scalable Large Language Models—A Research Agenda
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly transforming artificial intelligence applications, but their unprecedented computational, memory, communication, and data‐management demands pose significant challenges to existing computing infrastructures. Traditional cloud and distributed systems were not designed for the scale, dynamic execution patterns, heterogeneous hardware requirements, and service‐level demands of modern LLM workloads. This paper aims to examine how cloud‐native and distributed systems can evolve to support efficient, scalable, reliable, and sustainable LLM training and inference. Methods We conduct a structured analysis of representative research advances and practical developments in distributed LLM training, inference serving, cloud‐native orchestration, resource management, heterogeneous computing, and edge‐cloud intelligence. We organize the analysis around major system challenges, including computation, distributed execution and system software, resource management and serving, security and privacy, data management, and standardization. We further examine representative resource‐management strategies and emerging paradigms, including serverless inference, federated and decentralized learning, trustworthy distributed AI, and heterogeneous computing with emerging accelerators. Results Our analysis reveals that supporting LLMs at scale requires a transition from general‐purpose cloud infrastructure toward LLM‐aware, cross‐layer, and adaptive systems. Existing approaches have improved distributed execution, elastic resource management, multi‐tenant serving, and hardware utilization, but important gaps remain in cross‐layer coordination, workload‐aware orchestration, data and context management, interoperability, security, and system‐level optimization. Based on these gaps, we develop a research agenda covering future directions in sparse and heterogeneous computation, LLM‐enhanced system software, prompt and context management, autonomous cloud management, decentralized intelligence, edge‐cloud collaboration, personalized LLM services, and emerging computing paradigms. Conclusion Cloud‐native and distributed systems will play a central role in enabling the next generation of LLM services. Future infrastructures should evolve toward more intelligent, elastic, interoperable, secure, and heterogeneous platforms that jointly optimize computation, memory, communication, data, and service objectives. Continued advances in system design, standardization, and cross‐disciplinary collaboration will be essential for realizing scalable and sustainable LLM infrastructures.

papers.title: Nurturing a collective approach to Transformative Service Research: Improving experiences of an infant feeding service eco-system through service user collaboration.
papers.abstract: This thesis sets out to advance critical approaches in Transformative Service Research by employing collaborative processes to address research and service power imbalances. In doing so, I identify avenues for more meaningful theoretical and practical insights and promote increased service accessibility. The thesis is presented as three papers. The first paper draws on insights from user-led research literature alongside the analysis of 111 TSR articles to propose five avenues for progress towards a more collaborative TSR (more democratic research agendas, shared transformative goals, more inclusive methods, more transparent data analysis, and more accessible modes of dissemination). Through these avenues for progress the thesis calls for the reflexive application of TSR knowledge to encourage transformation within the research process itself. The second paper employs insights from a study involving a period of in-depth participatory research with users of an infant feeding service eco-system to critically evaluate opportunities to ‘walk the walk’ when applying the avenues for progress. Focusing on increased researcher reflexivity of positionalities, I assess the potential methodological advantages and challenges of applying an ‘insider’ approach. The third paper empirically evaluates data from this study, considering experiences of service accessibility. The findings reveal more nuanced insights regarding processes of value co-creation/co-destruction in public service ecosystems, focusing on processes negatively impacting user well-being. Extending Engen et al’s (2021) four dimensions of reasons for value co-destruction in public services (lack of transparency, mistakes, lack of bureaucratic competence and inability to serve), I substitute inability to serve for lack of provision, and lack of bureaucratic competence for failures of inter-professional collaboration, in addition to adding two further dimensions (barriers to identifying service gaps and failures and conflicting goals). Connecting these dimensions to structural influences, I present a framework outlining processes of value co-destruction in public service eco-systems. Thus, the thesis provides insights into socially contextual factors contributing to processes of value co-creation/co-destruction. Overall, the thesis enhances opportunities to prevent users’ personal decline in well-being in service and research settings through a deeper understanding of value codestruction processes and the advancement of user collaboration.

papers.title: Healing Landscape that Supports Healthy Ageing-in-Place in Suzhou, China
papers.abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid demographic ageing and extensive urban redevelopment in Chinese cities, ensuring elderly residents' quality of life and promoting healthy ageing-in-place have emerged as urgent social and urban planning priorities. Resettlement communities, which accommodate large numbers of elderly residents relocated from traditional neighbourhoods due to urbanisation processes, face challenges. These communities often lack adequately designed outdoor environments that meet elderly users' diverse physical, psychological, and social needs, thus limiting older adults’ outdoor engagement and overall well-being. Addressing these challenges requires not only an understanding of elderly residents' specific requirements for community green spaces but also evidence-based, scalable design interventions capable of adaptation across various urban contexts. This research aims to develop a systematic and context-sensitive landscape design framework to support healthy ageing-in-place in resettlement communities, with a particular focus on Suzhou, China. The study is structured around four core research objectives: (1) to investigate the relationships between landscape design, older adults' needs, and older adults' behaviours at the community level, guided by environmental psychology theory; (2) to evaluate current landscape designs in selected Suzhou communities using the conceptual framework developed from Objective 1, and identify efficient or inefficient designs; (3) to translate the updated conceptual framework into design prototypes that will be further refined through an iterative process; and (4) to develop and propose an updated theoretical framework and specific landscape design strategies that effectively support healthy ageing-in-place in Suzhou, suitable for retrofitting existing community landscapes. A qualitative research design was adopted to support the research-by-design process, comprising seasonal on-site observation, semi-structured interviews with elderly residents stratified by age and gender, spatial and environmental analyses, and iterative modular design validations. Fieldwork was conducted in selected representative resettlement communities in Suzhou, carefully chosen based on characteristics such as green space quality, proportion of elderly residents, and construction year. Empirical findings guided the development of a three-tier modular system — Basic, Standard, and Advanced — validated through focus group interviews involving elderly residents. The main findings underscored the complexity and multi-layered nature of elderly residents' green space requirements, captured across three core dimensions of elderly-friendly landscape design: convenience and comfort, social engagement, and spiritual richness. Within these dimensions, critical insights included the importance of seasonally adaptive microclimate management, accessible and comfortable pathways and seating arrangements, culturally meaningful and aesthetically pleasing vegetation, and interactive social spaces facilitating both casual interactions and intergenerational activities. Crucially, discrepancies between stated preferences and observed behaviours revealed a prioritisation of practical convenience and social accessibility over formal environmental qualities. Preferences also varied across demographic lines, with younger elderly cohorts favouring active, visually stimulating environments, while older cohorts prioritised safety, comfort, and ease of use. These findings emphasised the need for targeted and flexible design interventions. To address these nuanced demands, the study proposed a validated modular framework comprising Basic, Standard, and Advanced modules that integrate targeted strategies to meet different levels of needs across diverse communities. Empirical validation demonstrated their effectiveness in increasing elderly residents' outdoor engagement and enhancing overall spatial satisfaction. This thesis contributes both theoretically and practically by synthesising empirical findings, environmental psychology theory, and national policy standards (T/ASC 18-2021) into a replicable and adaptable framework to support sustainable urban regeneration for an ageing population. It provides actionable guidelines for planners, landscape architects, and policymakers, improving outdoor activity experiences for elderly residents and advancing broader public health goals articulated in the Healthy China 2030 initiative.

papers.title: DYNAMICS OF PORTFOLIO ASSESSMENT STRATEGY IN EVALUATING THE ENGLISH LANGUAGE SKILLS FOR PUPILS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENTS IN FAKO DIVISION, SOUTH WEST REGION OF CAMEROON
papers.abstract: This study examined the impact of portfolio assessment on evaluating the English language skills of pupils with hearing impairment in Fako Division, Cameroon. Portfolio assessment, as an informal and learner-centred approach, was explored within the framework of inclusive education, where traditional assessment methods often fail to adequately reflect the abilities of learners with hearing loss. The research utilised a quasi-experimental design involving pupils with hearing impairment in selected inclusive primary schools. Data were gathered through English language tests, classroom observations, and interviews with parents, teachers, head teachers, and the divisional delegate. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, t-tests, and regression analysis, while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis. The results indicated that pupils subjected to portfolio assessment performed significantly better in English language skills than those assessed through conventional methods. Statistical analysis (SPSS t-tests and regression) showed that pupils assessed via portfolios scored notably higher on post-tests (portfolio group mean=12.78 versus control=11.14; t(38)=2.919, p<.05). Regression analysis demonstrated that portfolio use was a strong predictor of language improvement (β=0.336, p<.001). Classroom observations and interview findings further revealed that portfolio assessment encouraged ongoing learning, increased learner engagement, self-reflection, and heightened teacher awareness of individual progress. The study concludes that portfolio assessment is an effective method for evaluating the English language skills of pupils with hearing impairment and recommends its systematic adoption within inclusive classroom practice.
